SpeciesNote.ahoggya: S&G: Strength +20, Dexterity -20, Intelligence -10, Psychic Ability -20; 1 in 4 is Anti-psychic. Eyes on all four sides: cannot be flanked; two blows a round on one side, four if surrounded. Charisma -40 with non-Ahoggyá, -60 with Shén.
SpeciesNote.hlaka: S&G: Strength -10, Dexterity +15. Can fly. Weak on the ground, skittish; will not wear armour or carry other than their own weapons. Charisma -20 with non-Hláka.
SpeciesNote.pachiLei: S&G: no talent modifiers. See well in the dark; 50% to sense ambushes and secret doors within 3 m when searching (30% when not). Four arms but one blow a round. Charisma -5 with other species.
SpeciesNote.peChoi: S&G: Dexterity +10, Psychic Ability +15, Comeliness +5. Two blows a round against one foe; excellent hearing; 90% to detect ambushes and secret doors when searching (80% passing by); sense living beings within 2 m. Cannot swim.
SpeciesNote.pygmyFolk: S&G: Strength -10, Dexterity +20. See in the dark; hearing better than a Pé Chói's; good tunnellers, climbers and swimmers. Charisma -20 with other species.
SpeciesNote.shen: S&G: Strength +20, Dexterity -20, Intelligence -5, Psychic Ability -10. May also strike a flank or rear foe with the tail each round. Rarely use bows; poor at sorcery. Charisma -20 with other species; cannot influence an Ahoggyá.
SpeciesNote.swampFolk: S&G: no psychic talent at all, so Psychic Ability is fixed in EPT's Non-Psychic band (no spells or sorcery; ancient devices can still be used). 1 in 50 is a psychic dampener. Sense 'wrongnesses' such as sloping tunnels and nexus points; natural swimmers and sailors.
SpeciesNote.tinaliya: S&G: Strength -20, Dexterity +10, Intelligence +5, Psychic Ability +15, Charisma -5. Intelligent, learned, good fighters despite their size; skilled with machines; very literal-minded.
SpeciesNote.hlyss: S&G: Dexterity +5, Psychic Ability +10. Powerful warriors and sorcerers; may strike a flank or rear foe with the paralysing tail. (Anti-human campaigns only.)
SpeciesNote.hlutrgu: S&G: Dexterity +5. Fight ferociously and never check morale; natural swimmers. (Anti-human campaigns only.)
SpeciesNote.shunnedOnes: S&G: Psychic Ability +20. Excellent sorcerers; can repair and recharge Eyes. Their stench requires a morale check of foes. Cannot survive over a week in Tékumel's air. (Anti-human campaigns only.)
SpeciesNote.ssu: S&G Grey Ssú: Strength +5, Psychic Ability +30. 20% a round to hypnotise a foe instead of striking (Ahoggyá, Swamp Folk and Tinalíya immune). The larger Black Ssú are Strength +25, Dexterity -20, Psychic Ability -10 instead. (Anti-human campaigns only.)

Nation.nlussNote: S&G Sec. 2.222 modifiers apply: Strength +10, Dexterity -10, Intelligence -10, Psychic Ability -5. Comeliness is normal among the N'lüss; with anyone else, S&G subtracts 15 from Charisma. They resist discipline and their morale is brittle in long fights.

Setting.name: Initiative
Setting.hint: EPT reaction time: one d6 per side (by token disposition), ties roll again. S&G: every combatant rolls a d20, again at the start of each round. A d6 each: one d6 per combatant.

Mode.side: EPT reaction time (one d6 per side)

Length.name: S&G: longer weapon strikes first in round 1
Length.hint: With Swords & Glory initiative, the first round is ordered by weapon length (pike first, dagger last), then by the d20. Uses the longest equipped melee weapon; no melee weapon counts as 'all others'. Missile users and casters not in melee are not bound by this: drag them in the tracker if needed.

Init.SideHint: EPT: each side rolls a d6; ties roll again. Sides follow token disposition.

PT.CasterLevelHint: Magic-user or priest level for its spells (EPT gives these as e.g. IV-XV). 0 = use its hit dice. Chance uses average Psychic Ability (table ruling).

PT.SaveAsHint: The 1975 rules give saving throws only by profession and level. Creatures here save as the chosen profession at a level equal to their hit dice (a table default you can change).

failedSpell.hint: The 1975 rules do not say whether a spell that fails its roll is used up for the day. On: a failed casting still uses it. Off: only a working spell is used.
failedSpell.name: Failed spells use up the casting

rollHP.name: Roll creature hit points
rollHP.hint: Each unlinked creature token placed rolls its hit dice for hit points (Sec. 710), and rolls its size first for creatures that come in sizes.

PT.SkillsHint: Professional skills are gained in order: a new skill must be the lowest one not yet held. Drag skills from the compendium.
